string.text:
%c[pda_white]Agony Mode%c[ui_gray_1] adds another layer of difficulty by preventing saves unless you meet the mode's requirements.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
You cannot save if you are:
%c[200,200,200,50]• %c[0,150,150,150]Injured
%c[200,200,200,50]• %c[0,150,150,150]Bleeding
%c[200,200,200,50]• %c[0,150,150,150]Radiated
%c[200,200,200,50]• %c[0,150,150,150]In combat
%c[200,200,200,50]• %c[0,150,150,150]During an emission or psi-storm

%c[pda_white]Life After Life Mode%c[ui_gray_1] lets you take over another random stalker after death.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Like the demon Azazel, you get a new body when you die. Your soul enters another random stalker who exists in the Zone.

If you have companions, you become one of them.

This mode is only enabled during character creation.

Every device uses its own batteries; without them it will not work.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
A small blue bar at the bottom of a device icon shows its charge. Devices consume power while in use and stop working when the batteries are empty.
Batteries can be inserted or removed at any time, so you can replace them when needed.
Power use varies by device; advanced equipment consumes noticeably more.
Check charge levels in your inventory and carry spare batteries when possible.

%c[pda_blue]Procedure%c[ui_gray_1]
• To insert a battery, drag its icon onto the device.
• To remove one, right-click the device and choose “%c[pda_white]Remove Battery%c[ui_gray_1]”.

%c[pda_yellow]NOTE%c[ui_gray_1]
L-ALT protects against accidental disassembly. This safeguard can be disabled in settings.

%c[pda_white]Campfire Saving Mode%c[ui_gray_1] disables quick saves and menu saves unless you are near a campfire.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
To save in this mode, simply stand near a campfire, then use your usual saving method.

This mode is disabled in underground locations.

%c[pda_white]Companions%c[ui_gray_1] are stalkers you can invite into your squad or hire.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
The Zone is extremely dangerous, so most stalkers travel in groups of three or four. This feature lets you do the same: persuade a squad leader to join you.

Requirements: the NPC must be friendly toward your character, their rank can be no more than one level above yours, and your squad must have room.

In some situations, NPCs can join you for specific quests under their own requirements. They do not count toward the companion limit.

Companion details are in the PDA's Relationships tab. There you can issue orders to the squad or individuals, and enable companion markers on the HUD.

Orders and behavior can also be set with hotkeys in the controls menu.

You can %c[pda_white]disassemble%c[ui_gray_1] various items to recover their base materials, parts, and components.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Disassembly is useful for clearing unwanted items and recovering components for repairs or crafting at a technician's workbench.

Three tools can be used:
• %c[pda_white]Swiss Army Knife%c[ui_gray_1] (not for weapons)
• %c[pda_white]Hair Clippers%c[ui_gray_1] (not for weapons)
• %c[pda_white]Multitool%c[ui_gray_1]

%c[pda_blue]Procedure%c[ui_gray_1]
Items that can be disassembled show “Disassemble [!]” when you right-click them in your inventory. Make sure you have the right tool, hold L-ALT, click the item again, and choose “Disassemble [!]”.

%c[pda_yellow]NOTE%c[ui_gray_1]
L-ALT protects against accidental disassembly. This safeguard can be disabled in settings.

You can %c[pda_white]disguise yourself%c[ui_gray_1] and move among other factions' stalkers as long as you do not give yourself away.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
To disguise yourself, wear faction gear (armor, suits, or uniforms) with the matching patch.
You can then move freely among other stalkers.
Stalkers watch you and your actions; a suspicion meter appears on the HUD to show the risk of being exposed.
Many factors affect disguise effectiveness and others' suspicion.
Check your gear's type and condition, act normally, and avoid unexpected behavior.
You cannot disguise yourself as a Monolith fighter; they use their own identification methods.

%c[pda_blue]Options%c[ui_gray_1]
• Disguise factors can be configured in the game settings.

%c[pda_white]Economy Modifiers%c[ui_gray_1] strongly affect life and progression in the Zone.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
They mainly control progression speed through prices for buying, selling, repairs and upgrades, loot rarity, cash rewards, reputation gains, and more. They are included in the game's three difficulty presets.

%c[pda_blue]Details%c[ui_gray_1]
Anomaly lets you tune progression and economy with these modifiers:
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Relationship Gain: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for faction goodwill earned from tasks.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Cash Rewards: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for money earned from tasks.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Repair Cost: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for technician repair services.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Upgrade Cost: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for technician upgrades.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Purchase Prices: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for trader selling prices.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Sell Prices: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for trader buying prices.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Loot: Items: %c[ui_gray_1]chance of finding items on corpses.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Loot: Money: %c[ui_gray_1]chance of finding money on corpses.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Part Condition Percentages: %c[ui_gray_1]show exact condition percentages for parts recovered by disassembly, making some gameplay harder.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Stash Discovery Chance: %c[ui_gray_1]chance to find stash coordinates in picked-up PDAs.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Weapon Wear: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for weapon wear.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Battery Drain: %c[ui_gray_1]multiplier for device energy use.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Consume Bolts: %c[ui_gray_1]bolts must be bought or found after use.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Artifact Degradation: %c[ui_gray_1]belted artifacts that protect you from anomalies gradually lose integrity.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Artifact Spawn Chance: %c[ui_gray_1]chance for artifacts to form in anomaly fields.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Trader Restock Time (hours): %c[ui_gray_1]hours until traders refresh their stock.

%c[200,200,50,50]WARNING%c[ui_gray_1]
• Economy modifiers are set for the current game.
• Change them only after loading a save, in the game settings.

%c[pda_white]Fast Travel (to Backpack)%c[ui_gray_1] lets you travel between locations using the PDA map.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Most locations unlock when first visited and then become available for travel.
A field backpack works similarly, but only for stashes you have created.
You cannot travel while in combat, overloaded, injured, or during an emission or psi-storm.

%c[pda_blue]Options%c[ui_gray_1]
• Fast-travel conditions can be configured in the game settings.

%c[pda_white]Gameplay Difficulty Modifiers%c[ui_gray_1] control how easy or difficult the game is.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Difficulty affects player damage protection, stamina loss, carry weight, thirst, and the need for sleep.

%c[pda_blue]Details%c[ui_gray_1]
Anomaly offers several modifiers to tune gameplay difficulty:
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Player Protection: %c[ui_gray_1]choose one of four presets for the player's base defenses.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Damage Multiplier: %c[ui_gray_1]sets damage dealt by ammunition from all weapons; higher means more damage.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Stamina Loss Multiplier: %c[ui_gray_1]scales stamina loss based on movement and carried inventory weight.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Maximum Carry Weight: %c[ui_gray_1]sets your carry limit.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Thirst Simulation: %c[ui_gray_1]makes the character need to drink.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Sleep Deprivation: %c[ui_gray_1]makes the character need sleep.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Daytime Radiation: %c[ui_gray_1]causes outdoor radiation exposure during the day. Protective gear helps only while it remains in good condition.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Radiation Sounds Only on Dosimeter: %c[ui_gray_1]when enabled, radiation clicks can be heard only with a charged dosimeter.
%c[200,200,50,50]• %c[pda_white]Anomaly Detection Sounds: %c[ui_gray_1]when enabled, entering close range of an anomaly triggers warning beeps.

%c[200,200,50,50]WARNING%c[ui_gray_1]
• Difficulty modifiers are set for the current game.
• They can only be changed after loading a save, in the game settings.

%c[pda_white]Guide%c[ui_gray_1] is a collection of information about gameplay features and the game world, intended to help when questions arise.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
It was added in response to frequent questions about settings, gameplay events, and mechanics, and also helps track your progress in a playthrough.

Articles are grouped by category, with key information available as soon as you create a character.

When a new article unlocks, a message shows its name and category so you can find it easily.

%c[pda_yellow]Disclaimer%c[ui_gray_1]
Since STALKER: Shadow of Chernobyl, this is the first serious attempt to bring back an in-game encyclopedia for all available content.

Although its features are nearly complete, the guide is still early in development and only a small portion of articles has been written.

Given its scope and plans, completion is still a long way off; some article categories are unfinished or unavailable, and interactive unlocking is not fully integrated.

More articles will be added with future updates and patches.

%c[pda_white]HUD (Heads-Up Display)%c[ui_gray_1] lets you monitor the current state of your game through indicators for health, equipment, status, and active effects.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
%c[pda_white]Condition%c[ui_gray_1] indicators show negative health or equipment status: gray means minor trouble, yellow means it needs attention, and orange or red means critical.
%c[pda_white]Danger%c[ui_gray_1] indicators show how safe your current area is and directly affect health and equipment; the worse the color, the more damage you take.
%c[pda_white]Current Effects%c[ui_gray_1] indicators show active boosts from items such as food and medicine. Protective and healing effects use different icons. The indicators fade as a boost expires and disappear when its duration ends.

%c[pda_white]True Darkness%c[ui_gray_1] is a special hardcore mode that changes the rules and activates the fixed Raid balance.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
It follows the original balance concept by Shabash.
Saving is unavailable during a Raid and works only in the Hideout. The game console and the “Load Game” menu option are also unavailable during a Raid.
Changing Raid MCM settings does not affect its systems; their default values are fixed, though all other MCM options remain adjustable.
If you fail to finish a Raid or die during one, all saves from before it are deleted. A new save is created when you return to the Hideout.
This mode cannot be disabled during a playthrough.
It unlocks achievements.
This mode can only be enabled on the character creation screen.

%c[pda_white]Map Markers and Locations%c[ui_gray_1] are PDA-map icons and areas that highlight points of interest.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Most locations and objects have their own icons and areas, making information easier to read.

%c[pda_blue]Toggling Map Icons%c[ui_gray_1]

Anomaly, important character and object, stash, and quest-target markers can be toggled at the top of the PDA map.
Regardless of these settings, moving objects and characters always remain marked to support clear navigation.

%c[pda_white]Rank%c[ui_gray_1] is a rating system based on a stalker's achievements in the Zone.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Most actions are recorded and award points according to what you do. Your score grows as you play, and your rank changes at set thresholds. Most tracked actions appear in your current character's PDA statistics.

Higher ranks unlock harder contracts with greater rewards. If you die in the Zone, your rank drops by 12% of its current value (adjustable in MCM).
%c[pda_blue]Ranks%c[ui_gray_1]
• Rookie: 0
• Novice: 75
• Experienced: 315
• Professional: 775
• Veteran: 1,500
• Expert: 2,500
• Master: 3,800
• Legend: 5,600

%c[pda_white]Reputation%c[ui_gray_1] represents how a stalker interacts with other characters.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Like rank, reputation is a progression measure, but it changes nonlinearly based on how you treat other stalkers.
The easiest ways to improve it are completing tasks, providing medical aid, and killing enemies of your faction. Canceling tasks or killing friendly stalkers lowers it.
Although some game features use reputation, it is not the same as faction relations.
The lower your reputation, the more others dislike you; those who disapprove of your actions may try to kill you.
%c[0,56,166,209]Reputation Levels%c[ui_gray_1]
• Vile: -2,000
• Horrible: -1,500
• Very Bad: -1,000
• Bad: -500
• Neutral: 0
• Good: 500
• Very Good: 1,000
• Excellent: 1,500
• Outstanding: 2,000

%c[pda_white]Stashes%c[ui_gray_1] are hidden places where stalkers store items, often well out of sight.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Stalkers leave spare ammunition, medicine, and food in containers, backpacks, and other hidden spots to collect later.
Owners often die with their stash information, leaving unclaimed caches with mixed contents.
Traders and information dealers may give stash leads and coordinates as a reward; desperate stalkers may sell or trade their stash leads to survive.
Create your own stash by right-clicking your backpack and choosing the relevant option.
Other stalkers cannot loot stashes you create.
%c[pda_blue]Identification%c[ui_gray_1]
Hover over a stash icon on the PDA map to see its type or status.
• Green: Untouched
• Purple: Unique
• Yellow: Player-owned
• Red: Emergency

%c[pda_white]Story Mode%c[ui_gray_1] provides several Lost in the Zone storylines in addition to faction questlines, which can be completed separately.
%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Ask your faction leader about rumors and the latest news to learn what they know.
This mode can only be enabled on the character creation screen.
%c[pda_blue]Availability%c[ui_gray_1]
• Loners
• Duty
• Freedom
• Scientists
• Mercenaries
• Clear Sky
%c[pda_blue]Additional%c[ui_gray_1]
Faction questlines are available to each faction when Story Mode is active.
Players in additional factions can also complete them by speaking to their leader once found.

%c[pda_white]Survival Mode%c[ui_gray_1] turns the world into a hunting ground where you are the prey.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Almost all NPCs are replaced by zombies and mutants that gradually close in on your location.

Zombies who have lost the ability to use weapons play a major role.

Only a few traders and stalker squads remain, so you must make do with and value what you have.

This mode can only be enabled on the character creation screen.
In %c[pda_white]Timer mode%c[ui_gray_1], you can save only after a set amount of time has passed.\nOnce you save, you must wait for the next interval before saving again.

%c[pda_white]Faction Warfare%c[ui_gray_1] simulates a war in which every faction fights to control the Zone.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1] You can command your faction using either dynamic expansion or manual control. Dynamic expansion adapts to bases captured manually when you switch back. Offline combat lets squads engage one another across the map, making the Zone feel alive and the war far-reaching. Dynamic expansion reacts to changes in the simulation, so each playthrough differs.

%c[pda_blue]Detailed controls%c[ui_gray_1] The PDA context menu is the core control system. Right-click a squad or territory on the map to open its menu, then left-click an option to issue an order. Player actions affect relations between factions.


%c[pda_blue]Smart-terrain types%c[ui_gray_1] There are four kinds of smart terrain: bases, camps, waypoints, and mutant lairs.

%c[pda_white]Base%c[ui_gray_1] Bases spawn squads and are especially valuable. The more bases a faction owns, the faster its squads respawn.

%c[pda_white]Camp%c[ui_gray_1] Camps affect the quality of new squads. More faction resources produce stronger reinforcements.

%c[pda_white]Waypoint%c[ui_gray_1] Patrol squads use these locations.

%c[pda_white]Mutant lair%c[ui_gray_1] Mutants spawn and live in these areas.

%c[pda_blue]Squad types%c[ui_gray_1] Warfare has three kinds of squads.


%c[pda_white]Defensive squads%c[ui_gray_1] Protect territories and other objectives.

%c[pda_white]Attacking squads%c[ui_gray_1] Are sent to capture territories and other objectives.

%c[pda_white]Patrol squads%c[ui_gray_1] Keep territories and other objectives secure.

%c[pda_yellow]Issuing orders%c[ui_gray_1] To select a squad or territory to command, right-click its icon on the PDA world map.


%c[pda_white]Select squad%c[ui_gray_1] Choose this option from the context menu; a marker appears on the selected object.

%c[pda_white]Select territory%c[ui_gray_1] Choose this option from the context menu; a marker appears on the selected object.

%c[200,200,50,50]WARNING%c[ui_gray_1] You can command only squads or territories belonging to your own faction.

%c[pda_blue]Right-click the player icon%c[ui_gray_1] The context menu is divided into sections according to what you select. The following options describe what left-clicking each entry does.

%c[pda_white]Player points: ########%c[ui_gray_1] Shows your current points. Clicking it has no effect.

%c[pda_white]Enable faction command%c[ui_gray_1] Your faction stops choosing new targets automatically.

%c[pda_white]Disable faction command%c[ui_gray_1] Your faction chooses new targets automatically.

%c[pda_white]Hide territories%c[ui_gray_1] Hides every object and smart terrain on the map.

%c[pda_white]Show territories%c[ui_gray_1] Shows every object and smart terrain on the map again.

%c[pda_blue]If your faction squad is selected%c[ui_gray_1] Right-click the player icon to send the selected squad to you.

%c[pda_white]Move out%c[ui_gray_1] The selected squad moves toward the player.

%c[pda_white]Attack%c[ui_gray_1] The selected squad hunts an enemy squad.

%c[pda_white]Move out%c[ui_gray_1] The selected squad follows the friendly or neutral squad you clicked.

%c[pda_white]Attack%c[ui_gray_1] The selected squad attacks the enemy territory you clicked.

%c[pda_white]Move to point%c[ui_gray_1] The selected squad moves to the friendly or neutral territory you clicked.

%c[pda_blue]If your faction territory is selected%c[ui_gray_1] Right-clicking a map icon lets you send squads from that territory.

%c[pda_white]Send squad%c[ui_gray_1] A randomly chosen squad from this territory moves to the player.

%c[pda_white]Send all squads%c[ui_gray_1] Every squad from this territory moves to the player.

%c[pda_white]Attack%c[ui_gray_1] A randomly chosen squad from this territory attacks the enemy squad.

%c[pda_white]Attack with all%c[ui_gray_1] Every squad from this territory attacks the enemy squad.

%c[pda_white]Send squad%c[ui_gray_1] A randomly chosen squad from this territory follows the friendly or neutral squad.

%c[pda_white]Send all squads%c[ui_gray_1] Every squad from this territory follows the friendly or neutral squad.

%c[pda_white]Send squad%c[ui_gray_1] Send a randomly chosen squad from this territory to your selected territory.

%c[pda_white]Send all squads%c[ui_gray_1] Send every squad from this territory to your selected territory.

%c[pda_white]Recall squad%c[ui_gray_1] Recall a randomly chosen squad from its target to the selected territory.

%c[pda_white]Recall all squads%c[ui_gray_1] Recall every squad from its target to the selected territory.

%c[pda_white]Target%c[ui_gray_1] If the selected enemy territory is a base, add it to the target list for squads at your selected territory.

%c[pda_white]Attack%c[ui_gray_1] A randomly chosen squad from this territory attacks the selected enemy territory.

%c[pda_white]Attack with all%c[ui_gray_1] Every squad from this territory attacks the selected enemy territory.

%c[pda_white]Send squad%c[ui_gray_1] Send a randomly chosen squad to the friendly or neutral territory.

%c[pda_white]Send all squads%c[ui_gray_1] Send every squad to the friendly or neutral territory.

%c[pda_blue]If neither a territory nor a squad is selected%c[ui_gray_1] Right-clicking a territory, squad, or map icon offers additional actions.


%c[pda_white]Send helicopter to point%c[ui_gray_1] Available when you own a helicopter; sends it to the selected territory.

%c[pda_white]Recall helicopter%c[ui_gray_1] Calls your helicopter back.

%c[pda_white]Hire rookie squad%c[ui_gray_1] Available actions depend on how much money you have.

%c[pda_white]Hire experienced squad%c[ui_gray_1] Available actions depend on how much money you have.

%c[pda_white]Hire veteran squad%c[ui_gray_1] Available actions depend on how much money you have.

%c[pda_white]Hire helicopter%c[ui_gray_1] Available actions depend on how much money you have.

%c[pda_white]Declare war%c[ui_gray_1] Available against a friendly or neutral territory only when dynamic faction relations are enabled.

%c[pda_white]Capture%c[ui_gray_1] Your faction can capture an unoccupied territory on its own. A countdown runs for N in-game minutes; when it reaches zero, the territory is captured. You must remain within the configured time and distance limits. Leaving those limits cancels the capture.

%c[pda_white]Send helicopter to squad%c[ui_gray_1] Available when you own a helicopter; sends it to the enemy squad.

%c[pda_white]Recall helicopter%c[ui_gray_1] Calls your helicopter back.

%c[pda_white]Become squad commander%c[ui_gray_1] With Azazel mode enabled, you take over as commander of the selected squad.

%c[pda_yellow]Additional information%c[ui_gray_1] The mode was originally created by werejew for Call of Chernobyl. The Russian translation and version 2.4 adaptation were made by av661194.

%c[ui_gray_1]With the required components, materials, parts, and knowledge, the %c[pda_white]technician's workbench%c[ui_gray_1] can craft equipment.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Equipment can be hard to find or buy in the Zone, so collect seemingly useless items and craft what you need. Depending on the recipe, you need:
 %c[pda_white]• Basic tools:%c[ui_gray_1] rare tools, but a thorough search may find them.
 %c[pda_white]• Manuals and recipes:%c[ui_gray_1] crafting knowledge, also found with other stalkers.
 %c[pda_white]• Components:%c[ui_gray_1] recover the required materials by disassembling unneeded items.

%c[pda_blue]Crafting Procedure%c[ui_gray_1]
1• Choose a category in the left panel.
2• A highlighted item has a recipe you know; select it.
3• Check the component and tool list; minimum amounts appear below the icons.
4• Crafting fails if tools or components are missing.
5• If requirements are met, select “Craft”.

%c[pda_yellow]NOTE:%c[ui_gray_1]
• Basic tools are reusable.
• Required tools: %c[pda_white]Rough Tools, Fine Tools, Calibration Tools, Medical Crafting Kit, Gunsmith Tools.%c[ui_gray_1]
• Tools already given to a technician are immediately available.
• Disassembly needs specific tools (see the Disassembly article).
• All recipes appear in the corner; only known ones are highlighted.

%c[pda_white]Technician's Workbench%c[ui_gray_1] can repair faulty weapons or protective gear by replacing damaged parts with ones in better condition.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Every weapon and suit consists of components and parts. Overall condition is the combined condition of its individual parts.
Parts generally have four condition levels:
• Weapon parts, worst to best: %c[d_red]Deformed%c[ui_gray_1], %c[d_orange]Damaged%c[ui_gray_1], %c[0,250,250,0]Worn%c[ui_gray_1], %c[d_green]Serviceable%c[ui_gray_1]
• Suit parts, worst to best: %c[d_red]Torn%c[ui_gray_1], %c[d_orange]Damaged%c[ui_gray_1], %c[0,250,250,0]Worn%c[ui_gray_1], %c[d_green]Intact%c[ui_gray_1]

To repair gear, you need:
 %c[pda_white]• Matching repair kits%c[ui_gray_1] (for the suit or weapon); buy them from technicians.
 %c[pda_white]• Spare parts in better condition%c[ui_gray_1], recovered by disassembling unwanted weapons or gear.

%c[pda_blue]Repair Procedure%c[ui_gray_1]
1• Meet all requirements. Once you have the required tools and better spare parts, the part-selection menu becomes available.
2• Select a highlighted part. The list updates to show spare parts in your inventory.
3• Choose a replacement part in better condition. It replaces the old one and improves the gear's overall condition.
4• Repeat as needed, limited by your spare parts and repair kits.
5• When finished, select “Repair”.

%c[pda_yellow]NOTE:%c[ui_gray_1]
• Inactive parts mean you do not meet the requirements, usually because you lack a replacement in better condition.
• If you have spare parts that are not in good enough condition, improve them first with: %c[pda_white]Multitool, Cleaning Rod, File, Basic Sewing Thread, Field Sewing Kit.%c[ui_gray_1]
• Each part replacement uses the matching repair kit once.

%c[pda_white]Technician's Workbench%c[ui_gray_1] lets you repair, modify, and even craft equipment yourself.
%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
Technicians use their vices and workbenches to maintain weapons, armor, and other gear and to perform modifications. Experienced stalkers often prefer doing this themselves, so many rent a technician's bench—you can too.
With an available bench and the right tools, you can:
%c[pda_white]• Repair (replace parts): %c[ui_gray_1]Weapons and protective suits consist of parts and components. Replace old or damaged ones with spare parts to restore or improve their condition.
%c[pda_white]• Upgrade: %c[ui_gray_1]Modify protective suits or weapon stats.
%c[pda_white]• Craft items: %c[ui_gray_1]Create items when you have the required components and knowledge.
When you use a workbench, a list shows the basic tools and whether they belong to you or the technician. These tools are needed for crafting and modifications.
An information panel at the bottom guides you through the required steps.

%c[pda_white]Technician's Workbench%c[ui_gray_1] can apply modifications to improve weapons or protective suits yourself, provided you have the required tools—no technician service needed.

%c[pda_green]Information%c[ui_gray_1]
The process is similar to a technician's service, but requires additional tools.
To modify gear, you need:
 %c[pda_white]• Matching repair kits%c[ui_gray_1] for the suit or weapon, sold by technicians.
 %c[pda_white]• Modification kits%c[ui_gray_1] for the desired upgrade and level; stalkers may carry them for their own use.
 %c[pda_white]• Basic tools%c[ui_gray_1] for the upgrade level. They are very rare because technicians keep them close, but can be found if you search thoroughly.

%c[pda_blue]Upgrade Procedure%c[ui_gray_1]
1• Meet all requirements and obtain the appropriate repair kit.
2• Select the item to open its modification tree, including upgrades already installed.
3• Each upgrade needs a specific kit with components shown beside its icon, plus certain basic tools.
4• Select an available upgrade. Repeat for any other upgrades you want.
5• When finished, select “Modify” to install all chosen upgrades.

%c[pda_yellow]NOTE:%c[ui_gray_1]
• Basic tools are required but remain available after use.
• Basic tools: %c[pda_white]Rough Tools, Fine Tools, Calibration Tools.%c[ui_gray_1]
• Hover over an upgrade to see its details. If unavailable, the tooltip also lists unmet requirements.
• Each upgrade consumes one use of its matching repair kit.
